 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. Chicago has been part of DeMar DeRozan's story in more ways than one. The former Bulls star also owned a mansion with a connection to one of the franchise's greatest legends .
 DeRozan purchased the River North property in October 2021 for $4.5 million. The six-time All-Star had joined Chicago two months earlier through a sign-and-trade with the San Antonio Spurs. The mansion previously belonged to Juanita Vanoy Jordan, Michael Jordan's former wife.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement The home has an interesting history of its own . Juanita retained the property after her 2006 divorce from Jordan. She purchased his share for $4.72 million in 2007 before eventually selling the residence to DeRozan.
 Located at 421 W. Superior Street, the Georgian-style mansion covers approximately 10,200 square feet. It includes six bedrooms, nine bathrooms and a five-stop elevator. Other features include a private theater, wine cellar, library and billiard room.
 Denver Nuggets guard DeMar DeRozan (10) Christopher Hanewinckel-Imagn Images
 A rooftop deck adds another attraction. The 1,890-square-foot space features an outdoor kitchen and fireplace. The property also has a heated three-car garage.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement DeRozan has now listed the mansion for $6.25 million, a $1.75 million increase over his purchase price. That represents a potential 38.9% gain before taxes, fees and renovation costs. The property is also being offered for rent at $22,000 per month.
 His time in Chicago helped make the residence another part of his basketball journey. DeRozan earned three consecutive All-Star selections with the Bulls from 2022 through 2024. He also made the All-NBA Second Team in 2022 after averaging 27.9 points per game.
 After leaving Chicago in 2024, DeRozan continued his career in Sacramento. His mansion now carries a new chapter, connecting his Bulls years with Jordan's family history.
